join.purpose: Have every agent, workflow and session begin from a recorded account of what this project's parts are for, so none of them rereads the raw project to find out.
join.function: Hosts the intake, knowledge, workflow and history modules over one shared record of namespace objects and receiver-owned joins, and hands each assignment the recorded account in scope.
join.relation: hosts the modules that record this project's functional account and deliver it to later work
join.observation: A module platform serves its project owner through the feature modules it hosts.
join.non_goal: Describing the project as it is written. The record states what each part is encountered for.

join.purpose: Get the project's functional account written from the project itself, then examined again by a second agent that sees only that account and never the code.
join.function: Runs the maintained Canonical Intake on the selected folder or file as a workflow, then runs the Latent pass on the retained Native account, each answer kept as receiver-owned joins with its own provenance.
join.relation: writes the project's Native account and later reasons over it in a separate Latent pass
join.observation: An artifact intake turns one selected artifact into a recorded functional account.

join.purpose: Decide which knowledge and memory reach an agent working on one element of the project, and hide or restore a layer without changing what earlier runs consumed.
join.function: Attaches layers to objects and joins, applies the mask rule from the project down to each element, hides inference that depended on a hidden source, and keeps agent memory as current revisions over retained history.
join.relation: selects which layers and memory reach each element's context
join.observation: A knowledge layer attaches to the element it concerns and is selected or masked at that element.
join.non_goal: Fetching context by similarity. Selection is by explicit masks.

join.purpose: Answer why an output, join or answer reads the way it does by following it back to the prompt and inputs that produced it.
join.function: Links each produced record to its producing operation, the exact rendered prompt and the exact input revisions delivered, then follows those inputs back through their own producers.
join.relation: traces each recorded output back to the prompt and input revisions that produced it
join.observation: A provenance trace names the producing occurrence of each record it covers.
join.non_goal: Giving authored, imported or manually edited content an invented prompt or agent history.

join.purpose: Keep the project as it stood when it was understood, and every experiment against it, so a variant can be rebuilt without the original repository.
join.function: Captures an origin from a folder or a committed tree, captures sibling variants against that origin, keeps content-addressed payloads, and reconstructs into an empty destination after checking file hashes.
join.relation: retains the origin and each variant of the project for later reconstruction
join.observation: An artifact history keeps an origin separate from the variants captured against it.
join.non_goal: Recording navigation markers or nonce files as edits to the project.

join.purpose: Add a feature by writing one module, as small as a single command, that uses the platform's public services and cooperates with other modules without reading their internals.
join.function: Offers settings, event, cli, data, work and modules as public services, lets one module call another's public operation with caller and callee ownership, project context and provenance kept, and gives built-in modules no privileged names.
join.relation: gives module authors one public contract shared by shipped and community modules
join.observation: A module platform gives every module the same public services regardless of who wrote it.
join.non_goal: Letting one module depend on another module's private engine, store or file layout.

join.purpose: Start from a working module that already uses every public service, and derive a smaller one by replacing its commands, settings, operations and subscriptions.
join.function: The standalone template runs by itself and shows synchronous start, asynchronous stop, settings, conditional commands, owned joins with revisions, jobs, nonce assignments and local events, while the event requester and harness responder derive from its lifecycle scaffold.
join.relation: teaches the module contract by running it
join.observation: A module template shows its platform's module contract by running it.

join.purpose: Learn what each module file owns and how the contract is used, in the module's own folder and at the point of need.
join.function: Each module carries a developer README that names what its files own and which chassis services it uses, and its usage help is declared in its own Python help contribution and shown by contextual CLI help.
join.relation: documents module ownership and contract use beside each module
join.observation: A module guide states what the module's parts own.

join.purpose: Receive exactly the prompt, context and submission header issued for one assignment, through any transport, and return an answer that lands on that assignment.
join.function: A nonce names a durable assignment. The exact stored prompt, resolved context, required header and recorded producer evidence come back for it, submission checks the header, complete settles the work and abort cancels it, and a working-folder marker only lets later invocations find the assignment.
join.relation: issues one exact assignment per nonce and accepts the headed answer for it
join.observation: A work assignment delivers the instructions it was issued with and routes the returned answer by its header.
join.non_goal: Judging whether an answer is good. The header routes the answer and does not grade it.

join.purpose: Work from inside an already-running Codex or Claude session over MCP, with several assignments interleaved on one server.
join.function: One stdio server carries the assignment, submit, complete, abort, call, status, namespace and resolve tools, every request supplies its nonce, and the server records its process id against each nonce it serves without letting process identity stand in for the assignment.
join.relation: serves assignment work to a running agent through tools keyed by nonce
join.observation: An agent gateway carries the same assignment operations as the command line over a tool transport.
join.non_goal: Replacing the command line. Every operation stays available there.

join.purpose: Be started by Metaform with the assignment prompt as input, without anyone waiting on the launch, and return an answer.
join.function: Runs a configured harness for an assignment as a queued job, with Codex and Claude noninteractive presets and a deterministic local fixture, keeps pid, nonce, prompt, stdout, stderr and exit outcome, and keeps an answer already submitted through MCP when the harness later prints its own.
join.relation: starts a configured harness on an assignment and keeps its outcome
join.observation: A harness launcher starts an agent process on a prompt and keeps what the process returns.

join.purpose: Encode a procedure once, with its sequence, branches, loops, waits and handoffs kept as authored, then run it, edit it, and rerun from an edit point while earlier runs stay intact.
join.function: Stores each workflow as revisable receiver-owned joins, runs prompt, user, tool, branch, loop, parallel and nested steps as durable handoffs, keeps object-bound references in prompts, retains the exact prompt issued at every step, imports XML, JSON and Markdown sources without running them, and reuses prior retained outputs on replay.
join.relation: runs the authored procedure in the order its author wrote it
join.observation: A workflow engine runs a procedure in the order its author defined.
join.non_goal: Adding approvals, retries or output gates the author did not write.

join.purpose: See only the commands that apply to the current project, module and assignment, and finish any task from the command line alone.
join.function: Builds menus and help from live module contributions, keeps the entered module across separate invocations through a working-folder binding, switches to the assignment menu when a nonce is entered, and offers a staged setup screen and scripted setting changes with the same capability.
join.relation: presents the commands that fit the current context
join.observation: A command interface presents the choices that apply to the current context.

join.purpose: Do the same work from a browser on any device on the network, without a second implementation of it.
join.function: One ASGI process per data root serves a main menu that loaded modules contribute to, the namespace graph and record views, provenance views and the workflow editor through the same operations the command line uses, and a token link signs each browser in with its own session.
join.relation: serves module pages and shared records to browsers over the same operations
join.observation: A web interface presents a system's operations in a browser.
join.non_goal: Being required. The platform and its command line run without it.

join.purpose: Open the shell, chassis setup or an agent tool from the browser or from the native terminal using the same launchers.
join.function: Configured launchers run in a pseudo-terminal owned by an operation, and their input, output, control keys and resizes stream to the command line or the browser, where the command line returns the launcher's own exit code.
join.relation: runs a configured launcher and streams its terminal to the CLI or the browser
join.observation: A terminal session carries a process's input and output between the process and a viewer.

join.purpose: Run a chosen set of modules and project knowledge on a machine with no installation and no network, including inside a hosted agent.
join.function: Builds one executable wheel holding the chassis, its dependencies, the selected module files and the selected projects' objects, joins, exact revisions and work folders. Direct execution against a fresh data root installs missing resources, keeps differing installed files and prepares native dependencies in an isolated cache.
join.relation: builds a wheel that carries the platform, chosen modules and project data to run offline
join.observation: A delivery package carries what its recipient needs to run without fetching anything.
join.non_goal: Installing anything from a network during a build.

join.purpose: Hold the whole product to one governing requirement set that every plan, matrix row and test answers to.
join.function: REQUIREMENTS.md states outcomes and invariants as REQ identifiers, REMEDIATION-MATRIX.md tracks work and verification against each identifier, and older specifications add no obligations.
join.relation: states the outcomes the platform must satisfy
join.observation: A requirement specification states outcomes without fixing how they are implemented.

join.purpose: See each requirement proven by observable behavior, with a passing test kept distinct from semantic correctness.
join.function: Acceptance tests run the platform with no modules, after module removal, from a cold offline wheel and across same-major versions in both orders, and drive the command line, MCP, web and browser pages from outside their implementation.
join.relation: proves observable behavior against requirement identifiers
join.observation: An acceptance verification exercises a system from outside its implementation.

join.purpose: Let a module be added, disabled or removed without touching the platform, with a failing or incompatible module unable to stop the platform or its neighbors.
join.function: Discovers modules in the System, User and Project places in priority order, reads platform declarations before importing code, activates each as one lifecycle, holds back same-name copies and lists them, honors the disabled list, and on unload withdraws every contribution while keeping settings, objects, history and provenance.
join.relation: finds, activates and withdraws modules as one owned lifecycle
join.observation: A module loader activates a module's contributions together and withdraws them together.
join.non_goal: Keying loading or commands to the names of built-in modules.

join.purpose: Give every module one object and reference model, so a module reads another module's records by exact revision instead of by private structure.
join.function: Stores namespace objects with receiver-owned joins, retains every revision, keeps immutable payload bytes, places storage in global or project files, and keeps object identity, revision and ownership when storage moves.
join.relation: holds every object and owned join that modules write and read
join.observation: A namespace store keeps each join with the object that owns it and retains its revisions.
join.non_goal: Deciding what any feature module puts in a join.

join.purpose: Run module operations and long jobs from one persistent host, so a client that exits does not stop them and no operation blocks an unrelated one.
join.function: One authenticated local host per data root runs operations synchronously or asynchronously, spawns jobs that end as completed, failed, cancelled or interrupted, marks jobs a restart abandoned as interrupted without retrying them, and cancels and settles owned work on shutdown.
join.relation: runs operations and jobs for all modules and clients
join.observation: An execution runtime runs work independently of the client that requested it.

join.purpose: Let modules cooperate through published events with inspectable delivery outcomes, instead of importing each other.
join.function: Publishes each event to its subscribed modules with exact join references in the payload, runs each subscriber as an attributable job, and exposes event identities and delivery outcomes.
join.relation: publishes events to subscribed modules and reports each delivery
join.observation: An event bus delivers a published event to the modules subscribed to it.

join.purpose: Give each module its own configuration that survives the module's absence and that hydration never overwrites.
join.function: Modules declare settings and defaults in Python, the platform fills missing values additively from those declarations, keeps glued values as user baselines, and stores everything under one external root shared by installed and portable runs.
join.relation: hydrates and keeps each module's declared settings
join.observation: A module settings store fills missing values from declarations and preserves values a user set.

join.purpose: Deliver each published event to every subscriber as its own job, so a slow or failing handler is reported for that handler and never blocks the publisher or another module.
join.function: Each subscription runs as an attributable job in the persistent host, and the outcome of each delivery is readable per subscriber, including the requester and responder pair that queue harness work and receive its response in a later event.
join.relation: hands each delivery to a job that runs the subscriber
join.observation: An event bus hands each delivery to a runtime that executes the subscriber.
join.non_goal: Becoming a second workflow engine that sequences steps.

join.purpose: Keep the producing occurrence of each write distinct, even when two operations write identical bytes.
join.function: Production joins are written into the shared record beside the content they explain, so a producing operation, its prompt and its consumed input references are read through the same join reference as the content.
join.relation: writes production joins beside the records they explain
join.observation: A provenance trace stores its evidence in the same record as the content it covers.

join.purpose: Keep an assignment's prompt, header, answer and delivery evidence as one retained revision, so reading a later answer cannot change the prompt a workflow already used.
join.function: The assignment, its producer, its submissions and its delivery evidence are owned joins with exact references, and a portable export rebuilds scheduling indexes from them and carries the work folder's files.
join.relation: retains each assignment as revisioned joins
join.observation: A work assignment is kept as records that identify their own revisions.

join.purpose: Serve the same assignment, prompt, references and submission contract the command line serves.
join.function: Each tool call resolves the assignment, project, work folder and producer for its own nonce, and call invokes only the module that owns that assignment, with background true returning a durable job.
join.relation: resolves every tool call to the one assignment its nonce names
join.observation: An agent gateway resolves each request to the assignment it names.

join.purpose: Launch work that another module owns while that module's workflow keeps ownership of the transitions.
join.function: Reads the exact prompt of the assignment, starts the harness with it, and submits the harness output as the answer only when the agent has not already submitted one.
join.relation: starts a harness on a stored assignment and files its output against it
join.observation: A harness launcher works from the assignment it was given.

join.purpose: Return to the caller at once and own the subprocess afterward.
join.function: Queues the launch as a background job, tracks the process it starts, ends owned children and drains their final streams.
join.relation: runs each launch as a job that owns its subprocess
join.observation: A harness launcher runs its child processes to completion under its own control.

join.purpose: Hand each agent step to an agent as one exact assignment and take its answer back into the run.
join.function: Issues each step as an assignment, seals the accepted answer so an MCP submission can feed the next step at once, and closes submission when an authored failure policy stops a run.
join.relation: issues each step as an assignment and reads its sealed answer
join.observation: A workflow engine hands agent steps to assignees and continues on their answers.
join.non_goal: Manufacturing an answer to a step that waits for a person.

join.purpose: Keep workflow definitions, runs, visits and issued prompts as revisions, so editing a workflow never rewrites what an earlier run used.
join.function: Definitions, visits, attempts and exact issued snapshots are receiver-owned joins with retained revisions, and an intake answer or an imported procedure keeps its source beside its interpretation.
join.relation: stores definitions and runs as revisioned owned joins
join.observation: A workflow engine keeps each run apart from the definition revision it ran.

join.purpose: Generate knowledge for each selected subject with the authored instruction, and regenerate only the subjects whose sources changed.
join.function: Prepares one inference per subject from the selected layers and joins, records a recipe with its sources, and reinfers the recipe for the targets that changed input references.
join.relation: asks the knowledge module for the context each inference receives
join.observation: A workflow engine that infers takes its prompt context from the layers selected for each subject.

join.purpose: Run the intake on the same workflow engine as every other procedure, so it has no second executor.
join.function: Starts the Canonical Intake definition on the selected artifact through the normal workflow lifecycle, and starts the Latent definition on the retained Native account.
join.relation: runs the intake as an ordinary workflow
join.observation: An artifact intake runs its procedure as a series of steps handed to a reasoning agent.
join.non_goal: Judging or rejecting what the agent answers.

join.purpose: Carry the intake's terms, method steps and response protocol as authored text that the workflow issues unchanged.
join.function: Canonical_Intake.xml is the executed definition, and its XML answer is imported so that elements and joins become receiver-owned namespace joins under the receiving element.
join.relation: issues the authored intake and imports its XML answer as owned joins
join.observation: An artifact intake keeps its procedure as authored text separate from the answers it produces.

join.purpose: Give the Latent agent its role and task without giving it the project's code.
join.function: The Latent role and task texts are issued with the retained Native account as the only context the agent receives.
join.relation: issues the Latent role and task with the Native account alone
join.observation: An artifact intake gives a second agent the first agent's account and not the artifact itself.

join.purpose: Keep the intake's answer as the project's account in the record, with the Native and Latent answers separately attributable.
join.function: Each answer is retained as a join, its XML is imported into namespace objects with owned joins, and the retained Native account is rebuilt from those joins for the Latent pass.
join.relation: writes the answer as owned joins and reads the account back from them
join.observation: An artifact intake stores its result as records that later work reads by reference.

join.purpose: Keep layers, attachments, selections, masks and memory next to the element they concern, so hiding or changing one never rewrites a record an earlier run consumed.
join.function: Layer, attachment, selection and mask records are joins owned by the receiving object, each attachment names its source join and its causal inputs, and memory edits add revisions to retained history.
join.relation: keeps layer and memory records as joins on the receiving object
join.observation: A knowledge layer is stored on the element it applies to and points at its sources.

join.purpose: Generate blind-spot and imperative layers from the recorded structure alone.
join.function: The blind-spot and imperative texts instruct one pass per property, and the agent receives the project's recorded elements and joins and no artifact contents.
join.relation: issues the blind-spot and imperative instructions with the recorded structure alone
join.observation: A knowledge layer generated from recorded structure is written without reading the artifact.

join.purpose: Keep each origin and variant under the project's own record, so history is exported, imported and inspected with the rest of the project.
join.function: Origins and sibling variants are namespace-owned joins, and their payload files are immutable content-addressed storage under the selected data root.
join.relation: stores origins and variants as owned joins over content-addressed files
join.observation: An artifact history keeps its records where the rest of a project's records live.

join.purpose: Carry a project's recorded knowledge with the wheel, with references that leave the project reported and not repaired.
join.function: Captures the project's objects, owned joins, exact retained revisions and payloads, the chassis-global joins they reference exactly, and lists references into other projects or missing objects with their reasons in the manifest.
join.relation: captures the project's records and the exact global joins they reference
join.observation: A delivery package carries each record with the revisions other records reference.

join.purpose: Ship the implementation of each selected module and no other, with each module's declared dependencies.
join.function: Reads the module catalog, copies the selected modules' files, and bundles the dependencies each module declares in its Python entrypoint from locally available packages.
join.relation: selects module files and their declared dependencies through the module catalog
join.observation: A delivery package carries only the modules it was told to carry.

join.purpose: Show one exact current snapshot of the namespace and its joins with their provenance in the browser.
join.function: Browser projections read the shared namespace service through the web module's public operations, imported XML is projected into graph data without inferring relationships, and each record can show its provenance.
join.relation: projects the namespace and its joins for the browser from one snapshot
join.observation: A web interface presents stored records without owning them.

join.purpose: Author, inspect and drive workflows in the browser through the workflow module's own operations.
join.function: The workflow editor and its HTTP adapters call the workflow operations that the command line calls, so a workflow edited in the browser behaves as one edited from the command line.
join.relation: edits and drives workflows through their public operations
join.observation: A web interface calls a feature's public operations and does not reimplement them.

join.purpose: Keep a launched process alive and owned after the client that started it disconnects or reloads.
join.function: The pseudo-terminal runs as a job in the persistent host, and the browser replays the job's live stream with flow control on reconnection.
join.relation: runs each terminal as a job whose stream can be rejoined
join.observation: A terminal session outlives the viewer that attached to it.

join.purpose: Show every public service working end to end in a package that runs by itself and is not needed by the modules derived from it.
join.function: The platform supplies settings, event, cli, data, work and modules imports that resolve to the active runtime and context without opening a competing store or runtime.
join.relation: uses only the platform's public services
join.observation: A module template depends on its platform's public services alone.
